question.text: Which of the following is NOT an obligation of the merchant banker in a buyback transaction?

answer.text: Ensuring the company can implement the buyback offer
Filing a due diligence certificate with SEBI
Determining the buyback price independently without company involvement
Ensuring firm arrangements for payment are in place

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Series IX page 222, the merchant banker's listed obligations in a buyback include ensuring the company has the ability to implement the offer, confirming firm arrangements for payment, filing the letter of offer and due diligence certificate, and assisting the company in determining the buyback price under the book building method. Independent price determination by the merchant banker is not among the listed obligations. The Trap: Ensuring implementation capability, ensuring firm payment arrangements, and filing the due diligence certificate are all genuine page-222 obligations of the merchant banker, so they cannot be the NOT-an-obligation answer. Note: Tie the answer to the explicit obligations list on page 222, which has the merchant banker assisting on price determination rather than setting price independently.
